transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-10 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (SummitDocs Eng Lead), Ethan Cole (Product), Marisol Ruiz (ML Eng)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/pocsummitdocs (deck), https://drive.google.com/sheet/benchmark-spreadsheet (benchmarks)

00:00 - Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick check, audio ok?
00:05 - Priya Patel: yep good here, thanks Maya.
00:18 - Diego Ramos: cool, i'll kick off with a 2-minute recap of where we left off — last week we wired the sdk into your ingestion service and you started exercising streaming, and we toggled the function-calling flag for one route. you hit a couple of schema mismatch errors and some unexpected tool invocation timing.
00:35 - Ethan Cole: yep and we saw the same behaviour on staging and locally, weirdly more frequent in staging.
00:48 - Marisol Ruiz: quick note, transcription today might flip model names — i wrote down redwood dedicate, it's Dedicated.
01:00 - Diego Ramos: ha, no worries. ok, technical recap: the SDK snippet you used was the beta v0.9.1, right? we have a patch in v0.9.2 that fixes edge case around partial function vectors and structured output enforcement.
01:18 - Priya Patel: yes 0.9.1. we didn't pick up 0.9.2 yet because of our deploy freeze for the week.
01:30 - Maya Chen: scope for today: 1) review logs from your test flows, 2) propose SDK/format suggestions for more robust function/tool invocation, 3) quick tuning tips (batching, kv/cache warmup), and 4) agree on next steps for pilot completion.
01:46 - Ethan Cole: sounds good.
02:10 - Priya Patel: i pasted three failing transcripts in the sheet, key issues are (a) functions return payloads not parsed into our JSON schema, (b) trailing tokens from model got appended to response causing a parse error, and (c) occasional 504s when sequence length spikes.
02:30 - Diego Ramos: okay parsing first: the function-calling path in our runtime wraps the function output in an envelope, but if the model outputs free text before the tool output the sdk parser can misalign. that's what v0.9.2 tightens — explicit start/end markers and a small post-parse validation step.
02:50 - Marisol Ruiz: is that the structured-output enforcement you mentioned?
03:00 - Diego Ramos: yes. we added a schema assertion hook in the SDK that attempts to coerce or reject responses that don't match the declared schema. we also expose detailed error payloads back to your logs so you can see token offsets.
03:15 - Priya Patel: can you show a quick example — like node and python? we tried to replicate but maybe our integration missed a flag.
03:28 - Diego Ramos: sure, i'll paste a snippet after the call — but in short: set function_call: "auto" and include functions:[{name:..., parameters: schema}] then on the SDK side set responseMode: "structured". that will prefer parsed object.
03:52 - Ethan Cole: the issue about trailing tokens — is that a model thing or a network truncation?
04:04 - Diego Ramos: usually model tokens. sometimes the model emits a short free-text note plus the tool output; with streaming mode that can arrive interleaved. There are two mitigations: 1) enable prefix/KV caching so common prefixes are served from cache and reduce free-text wandering, 2) set completion_stop_tokens and post-parse trim. Both are config flags in the YAML for the route.
04:30 - Marisol Ruiz: we saw the 504s when a client sends a 4k prompt with attachments, then the downstream reranker runs, and it spikes memory on the GPU.
04:45 - Diego Ramos: yep that suggests your batch window and token limit need tuning. For the pilot we recommended sequence_limit: 4096 but your current request combined system + attachments pushes past that occasionally. quick options: quantized model variant for that route, or route fallback to a cheaper model when request size > 3k tokens.
05:10 - Priya Patel: fallback is attractive — prefer cheaper for large docs where high fidelity isn't required. does that route fallback preserve user ordering/latency guarantees?
05:25 - Diego Ramos: yes we have routing policies: cost-first vs latency-first. when you fallback the runtime will call the fallback model synchronously; you can set async_fallback for background rerank if you want to keep low-latency path then replace result later. there's also an option to stream partial tokens while rerank finishes.
05:50 - Ethan Cole: back to SDK integration — we tried the function-calling pattern where the model returns a tool name and args; occasionally the SDK failed to call the tool because the 'args' field was stringified instead of JSON object.
06:05 - Diego Ramos: that happens when the model serializes the args as a string, yes. two ways to handle: enforce args as object in the function schema, or make the SDK attempt an auto-parse with fallback. v0.9.2 sets auto-parse on by default but marks ambiguous parses as warning level in logs.
06:25 - Priya Patel: could this auto-parse be a security concern? we don't want arbitrary code paths invoked or malformed payloads.
06:35 - Maya Chen: good callout. by default the SDK will not execute any tool handler unless you register the handler on the client side. the auto-parse only normalizes the args; execution still requires explicit handler registration and RBAC checks.
06:50 - Marisol Ruiz: speaking of RBAC, are audit logs created for every function call? we need per-user traceability for the compliance team.
07:00 - Diego Ramos: yes in Dedicated/Private we push an audit entry per invoke with token-level cost and trace IDs. Hosted has similar logs but you can opt-in for extended retention.
07:12 - Ethan Cole: latency — our main KPI is p50 < 300ms for short routes (<=512 tokens). how do your current bench numbers map when we enable structured output and function calling?
07:25 - Diego Ramos: structured output adds a small parsing step client-side, negligible server CPU. function-calling adds a few ms for the envelope and parser. the big wins/loses are model size and kv cache hit-rate. in the bench sheet I uploaded we simulated 80% cache-hit and p50 remained around 180-220ms on a gpus4-type node. with cold cache p50 moved to 420-500ms.
07:50 - Priya Patel: that explains the staging differences — our staging Redis isn't warmed so cache hit low.
08:00 - Maya Chen: action: Diego will document a 'warmup' checklist for KV/prefix caching and an integration checklist for SDK flags.
08:15 - Diego Ramos: noted.
08:25 - Ethan Cole: one more integration surprise: the SDK's streaming callbacks sometimes call the tool handler before the final 'function call' token arrives, causing early execution.
08:35 - Diego Ramos: streaming interleaving can be tricky. we added a buffering switch: stream_buffer_until_function_end which waits for function_end token before invoking handlers — default is off to favor low-latency, but we can enable per-route.
08:52 - Marisol Ruiz: can we toggle that per-route? we want low-latency on chat but buffer on background extraction.
09:00 - Diego Ramos: yes per-route config in the route yaml.
09:08 - Priya Patel: let's run a small experiment: route A (chat) stream_buffer false, route B (extraction) stream_buffer true. we'll report results next sync.
09:18 - Maya Chen: good. Diego, can you quickly show the high-level SDK flow we recommend for SummitDocs?
09:30 - Diego Ramos: yeah quick verbal: 1) register functions with strict JSON schema using the SDK helper, 2) set responseMode structured, 3) enable stream_buffer_until_function_end for extraction routes, 4) enable prefix/KV caching and set warmup script in the deploy pipeline, 5) set route-level fallback to quantized smaller model for big docs. snippet links in chat after.
10:05 - Ethan Cole: any gotchas with credential rotation? we want short-lived creds forwarded to lambda invokers.
10:15 - Diego Ramos: Redwood tokens can be short-lived via the private control plane; for Dedicated you can integrate with your KMS/HSM for rotation. we can also support signed ephemeral tokens for lambda invocations.
10:30 - Marisol Ruiz: we had an error where the SDK stamped an old API key into cached requests causing auth errors when token rotation occurred.
10:40 - Diego Ramos: that suggests the client cached a header incorrectly; we'll add a sample showing ephemeral token fetcher pattern and a middleware that refreshes before batching.
10:52 - Priya Patel: ok that should help.
11:05 - Maya Chen: quick recap of risks we need to mitigate before pilot completion: parsing mismatches, cache warmup, and occasional 504s from high token spikes.
11:20 - Ethan Cole: and security concerns: audit logs and handler RBAC.
11:28 - Maya Chen: agreed. next steps (recap): 1) Maya to send SDK snippets and a short patch notes doc (v0.9.2) 2) Diego to share warmup checklist and stream buffer config examples 3) Marisol to run the 3 failing prompts and log the function call traces and attach them to the sheet 4) SummitDocs to decide whether to enable fallback for large-doc route by 2025-04-17.
11:55 - Priya Patel: we'll aim for that timeline.
12:05 - Diego Ramos: i'll also upload a tiny benchmark run showing p50/p95 on cold vs warmed cache and cost per 1k tokens for quantized vs full model.
12:20 - Ethan Cole: thanks everyone. Maya, last thing — pricing/next commercial steps?
12:30 - Maya Chen: we'll email a summarized pilot addendum with proposed commit tiers for Dedicated and usage pricing for Hosted. i'll include an estimate spreadsheet.
12:45 - Marisol Ruiz: thanks all, meeting good.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and filler removed. Refer to shared spreadsheet for raw logs.

End of transcript.
